cause_quote: The new Darwin reader accepted unreadable arguments only when `executable && isForeignNativeExecutable(executable, uid) && native.isPlatformBinary(pid)` passed, so an unreadable foreign daemon outside that fallback caused the process census to fail.
user_saw: On macOS, `openclaw doctor --fix` skipped cleanup of eligible legacy plugin captures when it could not read the arguments of an unrelated process owned by another user.
summary: Doctor now excludes unreadable macOS processes with a known foreign UID from the legacy capture census, preserves foreign-owned legacy directories, and uses custody and installed-index references for managed native cleanup.
reasoning: The introducing diff shows that Doctor previously only reported legacy captures and that automatic cleanup shipped with a census that vetoed deletion whenever the Darwin reader threw. The initial reader rejected unreadable foreign processes such as third-party daemons and Apple app services, and I verified that #157102 retained that restriction. The host-wide census was extended to managed native cleanup later in #158414.
